messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: sustained error rate >30% on /v1/generate (hosted-api-prod-us). Autoscaler triggered 6 scale events in 3m (up->down thrash). Observed pod restarts and node evictions. Paging oncall-eng. thread: 1798765432

oncall-eng: I'm on it — acknowledging pager. First pass: check pods, node events, and GPU OOMs.

maya: I see a lot of CrashLoopBackOff on runtime pods (runtimes/gpu-*) across 3 nodes. Containers show OOMKilled in kubelet.

raj: logs from one pod: ```
2026-03-14T21:07:12Z runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
E CUDA error: out of memory (700) at inference.cc:452
NVRM: Xid (79) GPU page fault etc
kubelet: container killed due to memory oom
```

eli: autoscaler metrics show spike in qps per node at 21:03, then instant scale-up to add 4 new nodes, followed by scale-down within 60s. That oscillation matches thrash pattern.

sophie: ops-bot, can you dump the recent HPA/ClusterAutoscaler events and group-by-reason?

ops-bot: ```
Event: HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled up replicas from 20 to 40 (cpu target).
Event: ClusterAutoscaler launched 4 nodes (g4dn-like) due to pending pods.
Event: Pod eviction: node pressure (memory) -> eviction of best-effort pods.
Event: ClusterAutoscaler removed 3 nodes (underutilized) 55s later.
```

oncall-eng: Hypothesis: workload has transient token spikes that cause temp large memory KV cache usage > per-pod limit. Autoscaler reacts to pending pods, adds nodes, but cache warming on new pods causes memory spike and OOM -> restarts -> pods don't stabilize -> autoscaler removes nodes as they appear underutilized -> thrash.

sean: Are these happening only on hosted-us or global? I see EU region fine. Traffic routed from us-east, but fallback region has some traffic.

maya: Confirmed: all errors anchored to us-east cluster. Canary region unaffected.

pm-lisa: Customer impact: some tenants on hosted API experienced 5xx/partial responses for 6-10 minutes. Support ticket influx + one enterprise customer reported timeouts for embeddings jobs. Need incident severity comms.

raj: Quick mitigation options: 1) Pause autoscaler (set scale-down disabled + increase stabilization window). 2) Increase pod memory limit temporarily. 3) Drain/cordon offending nodes and restart runtime pods on healthy nodes with bigger mem. 4) Route traffic to EU canary while we stabilize.

eli: I can flip a CA flag to disable scale-down for 15m and set scale-up cool-off to 120s. That should stop immediate flip.

oncall-eng: Do that. Also bump runtime pod memory limit from 32Gi -> 48Gi for the affected deployment to avoid OOM during cache warm. We'll patch rollout as a single batch.

infra-runbot: Applying change: ```bash
# disable aggressive scale down
kubectl annotate clusterautoscaler redwood/ca stabilization=120s --overwrite
# patch deployment mem limit
kubectl set resources deployment runtime-gpu --containers=runtime --limits=memory=48Gi --request=memory=24Gi -n prod
```

ops-bot: Change applied. ClusterAutoscaler annotated. Deployment patched; rolling update started (maxUnavailable=1).

maya: Rolling update logs: new pods starting with higher mem; initial readiness checks pass. Old pods terminating; request latency back to baseline on a subset of hosts.

raj: Still seeing a couple of nodes with kernel GPU errors (Xid 79) which indicates potential driver instability under memory pressure. We're coordinating with infra to isolate those nodes.

eli: Cordoned two suspicious nodes to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45` & `ip-10-0-12-46`. Draining in progress.

oncall-eng: Good. Also enabling fallback model variant (smaller KV cache footprint) for high-traffic routes so in-flight requests don't trigger heavy memory use. Switching traffic gradually.

pm-lisa: I'll prepare a short customer status note: say impacted requests across hosted-us with retries/5xx, mitigation in progress, expected restoration within 30m.

sean: Any risk to Dedicated customers? Are they on shared nodes?

maya: Dedicated clusters are isolated; no signal there. Only hosted pool had the thrash.

ops-bot: Traffic steering update: `route-switcher` moved 12% of traffic to eu-canary, 88% remains in us while we stabilize.

raj: Post-patch metrics: 21:15 -> pod restarts dropped from 12/min to 0-1/min. Memory RSS per pod stabilized at ~36Gi after cache warm.

oncall-eng: Good. Keep autoscaler scale-down disabled and monitor for 20m. If stable, we revert the mem bump to a more conservative profile and tune cache eviction/limits in runtime.

infra-runbot: Note: nodes we cordoned show `dmesg` entries of repeated GPU page faults. Opening infra ticket to schedule driver/firmware investigation: INFRA-1427.

eli: Also creating a runtime ticket to add graceful startup KV limit and a pre-warm handshake option so new pods don't immediately allocate full KV cache. RT-567.

pm-lisa: Support message posted to customers. Will send a follow-up when we remove the temporary changes.

sophie: Oncall handoff: who's taking the overnight watch? We'll need a follow-up tomorrow for a RCA and playbook updates.

oncall-eng: I'll stay for next 20m. Then eli will take handoff if stable.

eli: I'll take the overnight rotation if it's green at 22:00.

oncall-eng: Final status at 21:42: incident mitigated, major thrash suppressed by disabling aggressive scale-down and increasing pod memory. Customer impact reduced; some retries/5xx for ~8m window. Follow-up actions assigned: INFRA-1427 (driver investigation), RT-567 (runtime pre-warm), CA tuning doc update.

pm-lisa: Filed post-incident comms draft.

sean: Thx team. Will capture timelines for RCA.

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: severity: P2; start: 1798765432; mitigation: 1798765800; stable: 1798766123. Incident channel will be archived after RCA. :white_check_mark:
